summary: the partition and root cases of tests/run parts on i686, against a reader that never takes a GUID table from its backup header, one that stops the chain of logical partitions after the first, one that truncates a GUID partition's first sector to 32 bits, a root by identity that takes the first of two matches, and an MBR identity whose disk id is not compared

argv: ARCH=i686 sh tests/proofs/guest.sh make rach2 && ARCH=i686 sh tests/proofs/guest.sh copy ${WORK} rach2/kernel

faults.name: backup-ignored
faults.summary: a GUID table whose primary header does not check is not read from its backup header, so the clone C has no partitions

lines: PARTSPROBE FAIL: disk 2's table from the backup header

faults.name: chain-cut
faults.summary: the walk of the extended partition's chain ends after its first record, so logical partitions 6 and 7 are not published

faults.name: start-truncated
faults.summary: a GUID partition's first sector is taken as its low 32 bits, so the 5 TiB disk's partition is published at sector 2048

edits.find: e = take(t, (int)i + 1, le64(entry + 32), le64(entry + 40) - le64(entry + 32) + 1, first,

lines: PARTSPROBE FAIL: /proc/disk: the 5 TiB disk and its partition

faults.name: ambiguity-taken
faults.summary: a root identity that several partitions match is resolved to the first of them instead of being refused

faults.name: mbrid-unchecked
faults.summary: an MBR identity matches by its entry number alone, without the disk id, so an id that no disk has names the first disk's partition
